subject: Synchronized tenor & onramp guarantee for Atlas Health renewal
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Synchronized tenor & onramp guarantee for Atlas Health renewal

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the productive conversation yesterday. Per our discussion I pulled together a structure that aims to balance your fiscal cadence with predictable unit economics as you scale. High-level proposal attached (initial-draft-amendment.pdf). Key pieces: 

- Term: 36 months (synchronized renewal date to align with Atlas fiscal Q1 2029)
- Yearly committed split: Year 1 = 25% committed, Year 2 = 40%, Year 3 = 35% (front-loaded support for ramp but protects Redwood unit economics)
- Onramp guarantee: 3 months of reserved burst capacity (covered credits) to absorb initial peak traffic without overage spikes
- Auto-renew: default ON with 60-day mutual opt-out window; we can make it OFF if procurement insists, but pricing will be ~6% higher if auto-renew is disabled
- Co-terming: allows alignment of additional projects under the same renewal window with simple addendum rather than full amendment

Ask: Could you confirm whether Atlas prefers (A) earliest go-live + 36mo term as outlined, or (B) a 24mo term with steeper year-over-year true-up but no auto-renew? Also let me know procurement timeline so I can prep an M.A.P. (mutual action plan).

I've cc'd Jordan and Ben to loop in pricing and account engineering.

Attachments: initial-draft-amendment.pdf (summary + draft language)

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference platform
From: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@atlashealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@atlashealth.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synchronized tenor & onramp guarantee for Atlas Health renewal

Camila —

Thanks for this. I like the general approach, but a few clarifications before we take this to procurement: 

1) Term: Our CFO is pushing for a 24-month commitment vs 36. Can you model a 24mo alternative and show what changes to unit price and burst credits?
2) Auto-renew: procurement will push to keep auto-renew OFF. If we keep it off, what incremental uplift do you need to keep the economics?
3) Security: we also need a SOC 2 attestation and the audit log retention terms spelled out in the amendment. Can you include a reference or evidence?

If you can send a concise two-column option sheet (24mo vs 36mo) that calls out price, credits, and operational SLAs, I can route to procurement and schedule a short 30-min sync next week. Sam will join procurement side.

Thanks —
Sarah Gomez
Director, Platform Ops | Atlas Health
sarah.gomez@atlashealth.com
+1 617-555-0912

Subject: Re: Synchronized tenor & onramp guarantee for Atlas Health renewal

Sarah —

Appreciate the quick feedback. I attached a concise comparison (amendment-options-summary.pdf) and a draft M.A.P. (MAP-Atlas-Health-2028.xlsx). TL;DR options below so procurement has a short summary: 

Option 1 — 24 months (procurement-friendly)
- Pricing: list price + 6% uplift vs 36mo baseline
- Committed split: Year1 40% / Year2 60%
- Burstable credits: 1 month included, additional credits available at discounted rate
- Auto-renew: OFF by default
- Notes: Lower term flexibility; higher unit price to offset churn risk

Option 2 — 36 months (preferred for unit economics)
- Pricing: list price - 5% (volume discount)
- Committed split: Year1 25% / Year2 40% / Year3 35%
- Burstable credits: 3 months included (onramp guarantee)
- Auto-renew: ON with 60-day mutual opt-out (we can set opt-out OFF only by mutual written agreement)
- Co-terming: Addendum path for future projects w/ no re-pricing in first 24 months

Security evidence: attaching a link in the M.A.P. to our SOC 2 report + standard audit-log retention clause we can include in the amendment.

Concessions and asks: To get to the 5% discount on the 36mo we need procurement to agree to auto-renew ON or a 60-day mutual opt-out window and a 30-day payment term. If procurement insists on OFF, pricing reverts to list + ~6% uplift.

Next steps: If you confirm which option you prefer, I will: 1) prepare a redline of the amendment; 2) open a DocuSign envelope; 3) add a one-pager MAP with milestones for procurement, security, legal, and account engineering.

Attachments: amendment-options-summary.pdf; MAP-Atlas-Health-2028.xlsx

Best,
Camila

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Atlas options — approval request

Camila / Ben — looping on the ask from Sarah. Quick internal notes (do not forward):

- Margin note: 5% discount across 36mo is acceptable if we secure auto-renew ON and 30-day payment terms. Otherwise the uplift conserves margin and I recommend only offering 3% + 3 months of credits instead of straight 5%.
- Alternative concession: if procurement insists on auto-renew OFF, propose SLA credit (0.5% monthly credit up to 6 months) rather than more cash discount. That reduces cash impact and preserves NRR.

Ben: your thoughts on technical deliverables for the MAP, specifically the timeline for SOC2 evidence and retention unusual requests?

Jordan

Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas options — approval request

Jordan / Camila —

SOC 2 note: can provide the 2027 Attestation (PDF) and a table of audit-log retention options (30/90/365 days). Technical team can support 90 days retention as standard for this plan; 365 days would require a small integration effort and a one-time fee.

Recommend we offer: 36mo, 5% discount, 3 months credits, auto-renew ON with 60-day mutual opt-out, and 90-day audit log retention (no extra fee). If procurement pushes OFF for auto-renew, swap 2% discount for SLA credit instead.

Ben

Date: Fri, 03 Mar 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synchronized tenor & onramp guarantee for Atlas Health renewal

Sarah —

Thanks for the input and for looping Sam. Based on procurement constraints and internal approvals, the recommended agreement is: 

- Selected: Option 2 (36 months) with the following confirmed terms:
  • 36-month term synchronized to Atlas Q1 2029 renewal window
  • Pricing: list price - 5% (volume discount)
  • Commit split: Year1 25% / Year2 40% / Year3 35%
  • Onramp guarantee: 3 months reserved burst credits included
  • Auto-renew: ON by default with 60-day mutual opt-out; if Atlas requires OFF we will document that as a mutual amendment and pricing will be list +6%
  • Audit logs: 90-day retention included; SOC 2 attestation provided (see M.A.P.)
  • Additional concession: 30-day payment terms in exchange for the 5% discount

Next steps: I will prepare the formal amendment redline and send a DocuSign envelope for signature. If that works, please confirm and I'll initiate the signature flow (DocuSign link will be shared). We've attached the summary and M.A.P. for your procurement and security teams.

Attachments: amendment-options-summary.pdf; MAP-Atlas-Health-2028.xlsx; DocuSign to follow: https://www.docusign.com/rc/SigningRequest?envelopeId=XYZ123

Appreciate the partnership — excited to get Atlas live.

Best,
Camila Reyes
